title: IP Addressing, Subnetting & Network Layers
beginnerExplanation: Understanding how data packets move from source to destination using IP addresses, CIDR notation, netmasks, and the OSI 7-layer / TCP-IP models.
whatGoodLooksLike: Can calculate available host counts and network addresses from CIDR blocks (/24, /27, /30) without a calculator
Can explain the difference between Layer 2 (MAC/switch) and Layer 3 (IP/router) forwarding
Can trace a DNS request, TCP 3-way handshake, and TLS session setup in Wireshark

title: Linux Terminal Navigation & File Permissions
beginnerExplanation: Mastering command-line navigation, file creation, searching, text manipulation (grep, awk, sed), and POSIX octal/symbolic permissions (chmod, chown).
whatGoodLooksLike: Navigates the filesystem comfortably without a GUI, editing configuration files in nano or vim
Correctly diagnoses permission denied errors and applies minimum required privileges (e.g. 640 vs 777)
Can pipeline terminal commands to extract specific fields from multi-gigabyte log files

title: Operating System Architecture & Virtualization
beginnerExplanation: Understanding the Linux and Windows kernels, user vs kernel space, processes, daemons/services, and deploying isolated virtual machines with VirtualBox or VMware.
whatGoodLooksLike: Can configure host-only and NAT networking for secure virtual lab isolation
Inspects running processes, open network sockets, and handles with system diagnostic tools
Understands the difference between virtual machines (hypervisors) and containerized processes (Docker)

title: The CIA Triad & Threat Modeling
beginnerExplanation: The foundational security philosophy balancing Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability, alongside STRIDE threat modeling to identify architectural risks before deployment.
whatGoodLooksLike: Identifies whether a given security control addresses Confidentiality, Integrity, or Availability
Can break down a web application into data flows, trust boundaries, and threat categories using STRIDE
Understands why security is a risk-reduction process rather than a binary state of absolute protection

title: Authentication vs. Authorization & Access Control
beginnerExplanation: Distinguishing 'who you are' (Authentication: passwords, MFA, SAML, OAuth/OIDC) from 'what you are allowed to do' (Authorization: RBAC, ABAC, ACLs).
whatGoodLooksLike: Implements multi-factor authentication (MFA) utilizing TOTP or FIDO2 hardware tokens over SMS
Designs role-based access control (RBAC) schemas adhering strictly to the Principle of Least Privilege
Understands Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) and how missing server-side checks cause data leaks

title: Applied Cryptography & Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)
beginnerExplanation: The practical mechanics of symmetric encryption (AES-GCM), asymmetric encryption (RSA, ECC), cryptographic hashing (SHA-256), and digital certificates/PKI.
whatGoodLooksLike: Distinguishes between encryption (reversible with key), hashing (one-way integrity), and encoding (Base64)
Understands TLS handshakes, certificate authorities (CAs), root stores, and certificate expiration
Recognizes legacy deprecated algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, DES, ECB mode) and replaces them with secure standards

title: Bash Scripting for Automation & Triaging
beginnerExplanation: Writing shell scripts with variables, loops, conditional statements, exit codes, and robust error handling to automate repetitive system tasks.
whatGoodLooksLike: Writes clean bash scripts featuring `set -euo pipefail` and meaningful logging
Automates log rotation, backup archiving, and automated user auditing tasks
Can parse system state and output formatted JSON or CSV reports for reporting

title: Python for Security Tools & Data Parsing
beginnerExplanation: Using Python scripts with standard libraries (socket, sys, os) and requests/httpx to interact with REST APIs, parse JSON, and scrape indicators of compromise.
whatGoodLooksLike: Builds custom scripts to query threat intelligence APIs (VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, AlienVault OTX)
Parses multi-megabyte JSON and CSV security telemetry with pandas or python stdlib
Automates port scanning or HTTP header security auditing using clean modular code

title: Log Analysis & SIEM Investigation
beginnerExplanation: Reading and querying security telemetry from Windows Event Logs, Linux syslog/auth.log, and web server logs within a SIEM (Splunk, Elastic, Microsoft Sentinel).
whatGoodLooksLike: Recognizes critical Windows Event IDs (4624 successful logon, 4625 failed logon, 4688 process creation, 7045 service install)
Constructs targeted search queries to track lateral movement across multiple host machines
Distinguishes legitimate administrative tool execution (PsExec, PowerShell) from suspicious adversary activity

title: Network Traffic Analysis & PCAP Inspection
beginnerExplanation: Capturing and dissecting raw network packets with tcpdump and Wireshark to spot unencrypted protocols, beaconing behavior, and data exfiltration.
whatGoodLooksLike: Applies advanced Wireshark display filters (`http.request.method == "POST"`, `dns.flags.response == 0`)
Identifies DNS tunneling, unusual TTL values, and beaconing intervals in captured PCAPs
Follows TCP and TLS streams to reconstruct application transactions and identify anomalies

title: Incident Triage & Response Lifecycle
beginnerExplanation: Executing the NIST SP 800-61 / SANS incident response lifecycle: Preparation, Detection & Analysis, Containment, Eradication, Recovery, and Lessons Learned.
whatGoodLooksLike: Applies proper host isolation without terminating volatile memory or destroying evidence
Documents chronological timelines with verified timestamps and preserved cryptographic hashes
Contributes meaningful root-cause analysis and preventive action items in post-incident reviews

title: Active Reconnaissance & Port Scanning (Nmap)
beginnerExplanation: Discovering live network hosts, open ports, running services, and operating system fingerprints legally within authorized test environments using Nmap.
whatGoodLooksLike: Understands SYN stealth scan (-sS) vs TCP connect scan (-sT) and UDP scan (-sU) mechanics
Utilizes NSE (Nmap Scripting Engine) safely with focused script categories (default, banner, safe)
Documents network topology findings systematically and avoids scanning unauthorized ranges

title: Web Application Security & OWASP Top 10
beginnerExplanation: Testing web applications for injection flaws (SQLi), Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), and broken access controls using Burp Suite.
whatGoodLooksLike: Interceps and modifies HTTP/S requests in Burp Suite Proxy and Repeater to test boundary validation
Demonstrates impact with harmless proof-of-concepts rather than destructive payloads
Provides developers with concrete, language-specific code remediation recommendations

title: Cloud Identity & Access Management (IAM)
beginnerExplanation: Configuring least-privilege policies, service account credentials, cross-account assume-role relationships, and guardrails in AWS, Azure, or GCP.
whatGoodLooksLike: Eliminates wildcard (`*`) administrative permissions in cloud IAM JSON policies
Enforces temporary credential issuance via STS/OIDC over long-lived static API access keys
Detects and audits public object storage buckets (S3/GCS) and unencrypted storage volumes

title: AI & LLM Application Security (OWASP Top 10 for LLMs)
beginnerExplanation: Securing generative AI and LLM implementations against prompt injection, insecure output handling, training data poisoning, and sensitive data disclosure.
whatGoodLooksLike: Treats untrusted LLM outputs as raw user input, sanitizing before rendering or evaluating in code
Implements strict tool-calling permission limits preventing autonomous file system or API tampering
Evaluates AI prompts for direct and indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities

title: Technical Report Writing & Executive Briefings
beginnerExplanation: Translating intricate technical vulnerabilities, exploit chains, and forensic evidence into clear, actionable executive summaries and developer remediation plans.
whatGoodLooksLike: Structures findings with CVSS scores, business impact statements, and step-by-step reproduction steps
Explains complex technical risk clearly to non-technical C-suite stakeholders without hyperbole
Delivers constructive, respectful feedback that empowers engineering teams rather than blaming them

title: Ethical Decision-Making & Legal Compliance
beginnerExplanation: Navigating the strict legal boundaries of cybersecurity (CFAA, Computer Misuse Act, GDPR), maintaining authorization scopes, and respecting responsible disclosure.
whatGoodLooksLike: Never touches an external IP address, domain, or API without explicit written, verified authorization
Immediately pauses testing and reports out-of-scope discoveries or critical PII exposure to leadership
Follows coordinated vulnerability disclosure timelines (90 days) giving vendors time to remediate
